Looking at the demo: 5s stay 5; each 0 becomes 3 exactly when there is a 5 both strictly left and right of it in its row, or both strictly above and below it in its column (all demo cells check out). The test uses colors 7/8 instead of 0/5, so I want to confirm the fill color before submitting.

{"action": "request_demos"}

Both demos follow one rule: cells of the background color become 3 exactly when there is a marker cell both strictly left and right of them in their row, or both strictly above and below in their column; marker cells are unchanged. (Verified cell-by-cell on both demos.) In the test, background is 7 and markers are 8.

```python
def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter
    cnt = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    bg = cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    colors = [c for c in cnt if c != bg]
    marker = colors[0] if colors else None
    if marker is None:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    H, W = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if grid[r][c] != bg:
                continue
            left = any(grid[r][k] == marker for k in range(c))
            right = any(grid[r][k] == marker for k in range(c + 1, W))
            up = any(grid[k][c] == marker for k in range(r))
            down = any(grid[k][c] == marker for k in range(r + 1, H))
            if (left and right) or (up and down):
                out[r][c] = 3
    return out
```
